speaker_role: student (self-reported admit to Harvard, MIT, Stanford, Yale and others)
commercial_incentive: None evident; personal stats-reveal video, no product or service promoted.
key_insights: Presents her full self-reported profile as a case study: near-perfect SAT, valedictorian at a small (31-student) graduating class, and nine AP exams all scoring 5, including three self-studied.
Argues her extracurriculars were the most important part of her application, built around a clear throughline in music (piano) and writing/entrepreneurship.
Founded and sustained a 501(c)3 nonprofit over several years (300+ volunteers, recurring senior-center concerts and fundraising) rather than a one-off service project.

Combined depth in one area (piano: 13 years, competitions, supplemental arts portfolio) with breadth across unrelated ventures (self-published novelist, cookie business, student government president, journalism).

Used the Common App's structure deliberately: submitted a music supplemental portfolio where allowed, and filled multiple honors/activity slots with specific, verifiable achievements (e.g., a named national scholarship, an Olympiad award) rather than vague descriptions.
Frames the outcome as holistic: she believes no single element got her in, but the combination of long-term commitment, leadership, and honest self-branding mattered.
Started her nonprofit and several ventures (bakery business, ASB leadership) years before applying, illustrating sustained multi-year involvement rather than senior-year additions.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Self-reported SAT: 1580/1600 (780 R&W, 800 Math), single sitting junior year.
GPA: 4.6 weighted, 4.0 unweighted; ranked 1st of 31 in her graduating class.
9 AP exams taken, all scored 5, 3 of them self-studied.
Self-published author of 5 novels, over 1 million words, 9 million+ views, over $10,000 earned from monetization.
Nonprofit she founded (since 2018) grew to 300+ volunteers, ~30 senior-center performances, raised almost $10,000 for disaster relief causes.
Cookie business sold ~1,400 cookies; social media videos of it viewed ~3 million times.
notable_or_distinctive: An unusually detailed, itemized self-report of a multi-Ivy admit's full stat sheet and all 10 Common App activities, useful as a single real data point rather than generic advice.
reliability_notes: Entirely self-reported and unverifiable (n=1 survivorship-bias example); presents correlation with admission as if causal ('this got me in') without acknowledging holistic/unknowable admissions factors.
